jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Sales Development Representative at Inner Peak
jobs.description: Employer: Inner Peak Expires: 09/27/2026 This position is ideal for a recent college graduate looking for their first sales role or a college student looking to earn a little extra money and gain valuable experience. We are a lean team trying to keep costs low. This role is compensated solely based on results - you will be paid per meeting you book for our CEO, as well as a percentage of any deal that closes. There is no base salary, and we have no flexibility on this. If you are not comfortable working on commission only, please do not apply. Summary: Inner Peak AI (www.innerpeak.ai) is blending new AI technology with human therapist expertise to deliver truly personalized, affordable mental wellness support 24/7. We are starting by serving high school and college students but eventually intend to be everyone’s mental wellness safety net, triaging users and delivering them to video content, human therapists, or crisis resources. We are a mission-driven company created out of our founders; own lived experience and struggles with mental health, and are still a small (but motivated) team. Peak’s founders met in undergrad at Harvard a decade ago before reconnecting recently over their shared interest in technology and mental health. We have built and launched a mobile application that has two thousand users and is live at several high schools. Initial student usage data is strong, giving us powerful case studies. To raise our next round of fundraising, we must scale this to more schools. We are looking for hungry interns who care about making a difference in peer mental health and who want high-upside potential through our performance-based compensation. This role is great training for anyone interested in going into sales, as you will report to a sales manager with 10+ years of sales experience. If you are successful at this role, over time it could turn into a full account executive role with a base salary. Responsibilities:You will be acting as a lead-generation sales representative for Inner Peak, talking to real potential customersYou will be calling private and charter school principals, deans of students, directors of counseling, and counselorsYou will learn to use Hubspot, the top startup CRMYour primary goal is to generate interest in Inner Peak’s solution so school leaders will want to see a demo of Inner PeakYour success will be measured in number of meetings booked for our CEO Qualifications:Preference for past sales experience - at minimum you must WANT to sellNo requirement for past sales experience (though it could help), but you have to WANT to sellYou must be personable, friendly, and not intimidated by cold callingInterest in / passion for mental health and / or K-12 educationHard-working, with the ability to put your head down and do callsA self-starter looking to bet on yourself You must be able to devote at least 10 hours a week during normal business hours to the role (though preference for candidates who can devote more)

jobs.description: Employer: Morgan Corp. Expires: 09/27/2026 Morgan Corp. is seeking candidates for a paid Equipment Fleet Management Internship for summer 2027. Fleet Utilization, Data & Equipment ManagementTrack equipment location, utilization, operating hours, and related fleet information.Review information from fleet-management, telematics, maintenance, and business systems.Assist with compiling and reporting equipment information.Learn how utilization, equipment condition, maintenance requirements, and project demand influence fleet decisions.Gain exposure to rental-equipment management, equipment assignments, transfers, and mobilizations.5. Technical Research & Problem SolvingResearch equipment specifications, OEM technical information, parts, attachments, and other equipment-related topics.Obtain and compare specifications, quotes, and supporting documentation.Organize information and summarize findings for Equipment Division personnel.Assist with investigating maintenance, utilization, or fleet-management issues.Identify opportunities to improve equipment reliability, utilization, cost, or support processes.Communicate with project personnel, equipment dealers, vendors, and other stakeholders as appropriate.Professional DevelopmentThroughout the internship, the intern will receive:One-on-one mentorship.Safety and technical training.Exposure to multiple Equipment Division functions and construction operations.Professional-development opportunities and performance feedback.Exposure to career paths in construction equipment and fleet management.Work Environment & TravelThe internship includes work in office, shop, equipment-yard, and active construction-site environments throughout North Carolina, South Carolina, and Georgia.The intern should expect outdoor weather conditions, uneven terrain, construction equipment, and active jobsites. jobs.title: Change.org, Elections Campus Ambassador at Change.org
jobs.description: Employer: Change.org Expires: 09/27/2026 Change.vote Campus AmbassadorAbout the roleWe're looking for a Campus Ambassador to help students on campus learn who is on their November ballot. Change.org runs Change.vote, a ballot guide that shows voters the candidates on their ballot, along with their policy positions and endorsements. Your job is to make sure students on your campus know it exists and use it before Election Day, November 3, 2026.You'll reach students through the channels that already work on your campus, including but not limited to clubs, campus-wide communications, tabling, relational organizing (talking to your own networks); whatever gets results where you are. We won’t prescribe one playbook; we're giving you a goal and will empower you to get there.Goals: Become the outreach manager for Change.vote on your campusReach as many of your fellow students as you can before Election DayCreate and recruit others for user-generated content on Change.vote and its social platformsGive feedback to Change.vote staff about what’s working on your campusWhat you'll doBuild relationships with student clubs, orgs, and campus communications channels to spread the word about Change.voteTable at high-traffic spots (dining halls, quads, campus events) to talk with students directlyRun relational organizing, asking students to bring their own friends and networks into the conversationTrack your outreach pitches and results and report back so we can help you troubleshoot what's working and what isn'tAdapt your approach as you learn what actually lands on your campusCommitmentPeriodHours/weekSeptember 21 - Oct 4 | 5 hoursOctober 5 – November 3 | 10-12 hoursWe expect roughly 55 hours total over the two months, with flexibility in the hours to fit in your class schedule and other commitments.What we provideTraining and ongoing coaching on tactics, messaging, and troubleshootingYou’ll be part of a cohort of Change.vote campus ambassadors across our two statesMaterials, talking points, and campus-vote tools you can adapt to what works locallyA direct line to our team for support, not a script to follow blindlyWho this is forThis is a great fit if you want real civic engagement experience like organizing, communications, relationship-building, without working for a candidate or campaign. It's nonpartisan work: you're helping students find accurate information about their ballot, not telling them how to vote.We're looking for someone who:Is plugged into their campus community (or eager to get plugged in)Is comfortable talking to strangers and building relationshipsCan work independently and adapt tactics without needing a rigid scriptCares about voter turnout and access to information, regardless of partyCompensation$1500 Stipend with half paid after Sept. 30 and the remaining paid at the conclusion of the contract/agreement. Cost coverage for printed materials or tabling fees associated with outreach.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Engineering Intern (Spring 2027) at SRC, Inc
jobs.description: Employer: SRC, Inc Expires: 09/27/2026 SRC Inc. is seeking Engineering Interns for spring 2027 who will be working onsite, 40 hours a week. As an engineering intern, you will contribute to the design, development, implementation and testing of state-of-the-art radar and electronic warfare products. Based on your interests, you will be selected to work in one specialization from Embedded Design, Machine Intelligence, Integration & Test Engineering, or Software Engineering. You will work closely with senior engineers and gain experience in creating innovative solutions tailored to our products and customer needs. You will bring your unique perspective to our multi-department teams of engineers and collaborate on designs aligned with project goals and requirements. What You'll Do Embedded Design: * Design, develop, implement, test and optimize firmware using VHDL/Verilog * Work with FPGAs and System-on-Chips (SoCs) to develop electronic warfare and radar systems * Learn and apply FPGA design principles including RTL design, verification, logic synthesis, prototyping, and timing analysis * Use Python, TCL and other scripting languages to automate continuous development, continuous integration (CI/CD) workflows Software Engineer: * Design and develop high-quality software solutions using an Agile workflow * Write clean, efficient code and participate in code reviews to ensure delivery of quality products * Communicate proposed software solutions with multi-department engineering teams. * Develop sound software engineering principles using tools such as Git, Bamboo, Sonarqube * Adapt to new technologies and languages including Docker, Kubernetes, Rust as program needs allow Machine Intelligence Engineer: * Develop machine learning algorithms and models to enhance product capabilities * Analyze data to identify patterns and optimize decision-making processes * Work with software and hardware teams to integrate AI/ML solutions into products Integration & Test Engineer: * Participate in design requirements reviews to ensure the requirements can be tested * Coordinate integration of subsystems and components into full systems. * Develop, execute and troubleshoot test plans and procedures to validate system functionality. * Increase testing efficiency by utilizing Python-based automated test suite. * Utilize model-based tools to define test strategies and verifications against system designs What You'll Bring * Completion of two years of college and current enrollment in a bachelor's degree in a relevant engineering field (e.g., Electrical, Computer, Computer Science, or Software) * A minimum grade point average of 3.3. Most recent transcripts are required with application (unofficial transcripts are acceptable) * A strong understanding of your engineering fields foundational concepts * Knowledge of design, testing, and debugging techniques relevant to your field * Ability to take initiative and proactively address challenges * Familiarity with applicable tools and methodologies * Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment with excellent communication skills What Sets Us Apart?SRC, Inc., a not-for-profit research and development company, combines information, science, technology and ingenuity to solve "impossible" problems in the areas of defense, environment and intelligence. Across our family of companies, we apply bright minds, fresh thinking and relentless determination to deliver innovative products and services that areredefining possible®. When you join our team, you'll be a part of something truly meaningful - helping to keep America and its allies safe and strong. You'll collaborate with more than 1,400 engineers, scientists and professionals - with 20 percent of those employees having served in the military - in a highly innovative, inclusive and equitable work environment. You'll receive a competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package that includes four or more weeks of paid time off to start, 10 percent employer contribution toward retirement, and 100 percent tuition support. Total compensation for this role is market competitive. The anticipated range for this position based out of Syracuse, NY is estimated at $22.00 to $26.00/hour. The actual salary will vary based on applicant's experience, skills, and abilities, geographic location as well as other business and organizational needs. SRC offers competitive benefit options, for more details please visit our website. Non-Discrimination Statement Individuals seeking employment are considered without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or age, or status as a protected veteran or disability except as strictly required by applicable law. You are being given the opportunity to provide the following information in order to help us comply with federal and state record keeping, reporting, and other legal requirements, including requirements under Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act, 29 U.S.C. 793, and the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act (VEVRAA), 38 U.S.C. 4212.Learn more about SRC: About UsEmployee BenefitsAwards & RecognitionSecurity Clearance * Location Syracuse, New York

jobs.title: Summer Analyst, Americas Asset Management - New York City - 3 Months at QuadReal
jobs.description: Employer: QuadReal Expires: 09/27/2026 At QuadReal, excellence lives here! We are committed to providing our Co-ops/Interns with a student experience that provides a supportive and engaging learning environment while developing skills and business acumen. Students will have the opportunity to participate in a variety of experiences including our Corporate Speaker Series, Fireside Chats, Volunteer opportunities and Networking events. Eligibility Note: To qualify for a student (Co-op/Internship) opportunity, students must be enrolled in their academic studies at a post-secondary institution (university/college) and must be returning to school after completion of their work term with QuadReal. If you are a student registered in an official co-op program at your post-secondary institution and completion of a final work term is a mandatory component for you to graduate, you are eligible to apply with the understanding that you will leave QuadReal at the end of your work term or have the possibility to be considered for full-time opportunities. We are actively looking for a Summer Analyst, Americas Asset Management to join our team in Summer 2027. This position will be based in New York City and will report directly to the Associate, Americas Asset Management. This role will support QuadReal’s Americas Asset Management team by assisting in the execution of comprehensive asset strategies, providing analytical support for multiple asset types across QuadReal’s U.S. portfolio, including Residential, Industrial, Office, and Alternative Asset Class properties. What We Offer: An organization and leaders that support your development through meaningful work experience A Student Mentorship Program designed to provide support throughout your experience Opportunities to build your industry knowledge through weekly Speaker Series & Fireside Chats Opportunities to participate in case competitions within QuadReal during your work term, fostering cross-functional collaboration with intern peers and enhancing exposure to real-world problem-solving. Giving back to the community with your peers and team members through volunteering events Opportunities to build long-lasting industry and professional relationships What You Will Experience: Understand and be exposed to all aspects of the real estate lifecycle — including development/construction, property operations, business plans, budget implementation, and financing/disposition activities. Develop a working knowledge of partnership agreements, development agreements, construction agreements, property management agreements, and other agreements to assist with project tracking and oversight responsibilities. Assist in the monitoring of existing investments/joint ventures, including maintaining cash flow and valuation models. Analyze project sustainability, wellness, and smart building specifications against programmatic goals and portfolio wide performance benchmarks.Assist with monthly and quarterly reporting, construction progress metrics, operating performance measurements, and other KPIs. Work with multiple teams to audit and maintain proprietary databases and reporting dashboards for accurate and timely reporting. What You Will Bring: Education – Completing a university degree with a major in Real Estate, Real Estate Development, Real Estate Finance and Investment Construction Management. Pursuing a graduate degree in one of these fields is an asset. Analytical – Strong quantitative and analytical skills; detail-oriented and proficient in building and handling complicated data sets. Communication – Excellent communication and presentation skills; demonstrate an ability to effectively communicate and present results that articulate key themes and messages. Organization – Must be able to allocate time effectively and work under pressure to meet tight deadlines, handle multiple demands and competing priorities, and adapt to new ideas and change. Comfortable following direction but also contributing to the direction. Software – Must have advanced knowledge of Excel, PowerPoint and Word; knowledge of Argus or Yardi an asset. Familiarity with AI-enabled tools to support research, analysis, or productivity is considered an asset. Relationship – Must be extremely proactive and work well in a collaborative environment, with the ability to take guidance but then move projects forward independently. Values – Embrace and pro-actively support QuadReal’s values and its culture of environmental sustainability and corporate and social responsibility. Experience – Previous experience in real estate investment, asset management, development, construction oversight, architecture, or engineering. Understanding of real estate fundamentals and project finance along with investment and asset management practices and the full cycle of project planning, design, and execution. The expected hourly rate for this role is $36. About QuadReal Property Group QuadReal Property Group is a global real estate investment, development and operating company headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia. Its assets under management are $98.5 billion. From its foundation in Canada as a full-service real estate operating company, QuadReal has expanded its capabilities globally for investments in equity and debt in both the public and private markets. QuadReal invests directly through operating platforms in which it holds an ownership interest and via programmatic partnerships. QuadReal seeks to deliver strong investment returns while creating sustainable environments that bring value to the people and communities it serves. Now and for generations to come. QuadReal: Excellence lives here. www.quadreal.com The actual salary offered will take into consideration a wide array of factors including, but not limited to, the individual’s skill, experience, education and training, the market compensation of the role, and the consideration to internal equity. We value diverse experiences and perspectives. Even if your skills don’t align 100% with the listed qualifications or salary range, we encourage you to apply – you may be a great fit for this role or others in our community. Applicants may also be considered for alternative positions within the organization where their qualifications and experience align more closely with available opportunities. We use artificial intelligence (AI) technology — alongside human review — to assist in screening and assessing applicants for this position. Our recruitment team remains involved in all decisions. Note to Recruiters: QuadReal does not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than directly from a candidate. Any unsolicited resumes sent to QuadReal, directly or indirectly, will be considered QuadReal property. QuadReal will not pay a fee for any placement resulting from the receipt of an unsolicited resume. A recruiting agency must first have a valid, written and fully executed agency agreement contract for engaged services to submit resumes. QuadReal will provide reasonable accommodation at any time throughout the hiring process for applicants with disabilities or for those needing job postings in an alternate format. If you require accommodation, please advise the Talent Acquisition team member you are working with and include the following: Job posting #, your name and your preferred method of contact.

Key ResponsibilitiesAssist in planning, scheduling, and coordinating mechanical projects.Provide support for reviewing designs, drawings, and specifications.Assist with managing project documentation, including submittals, RFIs, change orders, and reports.Participate in site visits to monitor progress and ensure compliance with specifications.Support the preparation of cost estimates and budgets.Aid in the implementation of quality control measures.Facilitate communication among project teams, subcontractors, suppliers, and clients.Assist with safety protocol implementation and compliance. QualificationsRequiredMust be currently enrolled in an accredited university program and actively pursuing a degree in Construction Management, Mechanical Engineering or related field.Proficiency in computer programs such as Microsoft Office Products (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook, etc.).Demonstrated ability to take initiative and interact effectively in a team environment.Availability to work 40 hours per week within the required schedule for the duration of the internship (typically 10 weeks).PreferredStrong organizational skills.Ability to multi-task and work in a fast-paced environment.Experience with construction software such as Revit, Navisworks, Bluebeam, Procore, ACC Build or other related programs. Physical RequirementsProlonged periods of sitting at a desk.Must be able to lift to 15 pounds at times.Must have sufficient visual acuity to view and interpret detailed construction drawings on computer screens and on paper.Must be able to traverse uneven surfaces on project sites and climb stairs to access project site temporary offices. Contingent EmploymentOffers of employment are contingent upon successful completion of the Company’s required pre-employment drug screening process. Murray Company is a federal contractor and complies with all applicable federal laws and regulations regarding controlled substances. Work AuthorizationMurray Company is not sponsoring employment-based visas at this time. Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on an ongoing, permanent basis without the need for current or future visa sponsorship.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Business Analyst Intern at Right Click
jobs.description: Employer: Right Click Expires: 09/27/2026 Consulting is finally reaching small and medium businesses.Strategy consulting has long had a price floor. A partner sold the work, and a pyramid of analysts did the research, the document review, the benchmarking, the models, the first drafts. That pyramid is roughly why serious advisory work tended to start around $100,000, which left the small and mid-sized businesses that make up most of the economy largely outside the market.That's starting to change. Analytical work that would have taken weeks can now often be done by a agile team with a good AI workflow. It starts to look possible to deliver real advisory work to a 60-person manufacturer in Orange County at a price they'd actually pay.We're a managed IT and cybersecurity firm working with clients across aerospace, defense, healthcare, and professional services in Southern California. We already have the relationships, and we have an unusual amount of data — years of ticket history, systems inventory, security posture, and software spend for every client we serve. It's close to the raw material an outside consultant would spend weeks trying to assemble. We're building a consulting practice that turns that operational data into recommendations clients can act on.What you'd actually doYou'd take a live client, pull their operational data, and look for the story in it — where money is leaking, which systems have quietly become shelfware, what's generating the same ticket forty times a month, where they might be exposed on compliance. Then you'd build the analysis and write up the recommendation.The intent is that your work, with your name on it, shapes what we end up advising a client to do, rather than arriving as a research task with the interesting part already decided.What you leave withA portfolio of real client work, which not many interns get. Real fluency in AI-assisted analysis — a competence a lot of firms are hiring for and most programs haven't caught up to yet. And some sense of what it looks like to build a business model from the inside, which is a different education than a semester of cases about someone else's.We're looking forA business, finance, economics, or analytics student who's curious about how companies actually run, reasonably comfortable with messy data and Excel, and a clear writer. It helps if you've already been using Claude or similar AI tools on your own coursework and have some feel for where they're genuinely useful and where they aren't. More than any of that, we're looking for someone who wants to go find the answer rather than wait to be handed the question.ApplySend a résumé and a short note — three or four sentences on a business problem you've found interesting lately — to [careers@rclick.com].Right Click is an equal opportunity employer.Benefits:401(k)401(k) matchingDental insuranceEmployee assistance programFlexible spending accountHealth insurancePaid time offProfessional development assistanceRetirement planVision insuranceWork Location: In person

jobs.description: Employer: Grant Thornton Expires: 09/27/2026 Please apply to the position/location you are most interested in. In order to be considered for this position you must: 1. Apply through the Grant Thornton Job portal at www.grantthornton.com/campuscareers (including resume and transcript) Who is Grant Thornton? At Grant Thornton, we believe in making business more personal and building trust into every result – for our clients and you. Here, we go beyond your expectations of a career in professional services by offering a career path with more: more opportunity, more flexibility, and more support. It’s what makes us different, and we think being different makes us better. In the U.S., Grant Thornton delivers professional services through two specialized entities: Grant Thornton LLP, a licensed, certified public accounting (CPA) firm that provides audit and assurance services ― and Grant Thornton Advisors LLC (not a licensed CPA firm), which exclusively provides non-attest offerings, including tax and advisory services. In 2025, Grant Thornton formed a multinational, multidisciplinary platform with Grant Thornton Ireland. The platform offers a premier Trans-Atlantic advisory and tax practice, as well as independent American and Irish audit practices. With $2.7 billion in revenues and more than 50 offices spanning the U.S., Ireland and other territories, the platform delivers a singular client experience that includes enhanced solutions and capabilities, backed by powerful technologies and a roster of 12,000 quality-driven professionals enjoying exceptional career-growth opportunities and a distinctive cross-border culture. Grant Thornton is part of the Grant Thornton International Limited network, which provides access to its member firms in more than 150 global markets. Our advisory practice creates holistic solutions delivered by innovative, curious professionals who bring technical depth and industry insight to our clients. What is Risk Advisory? Within our Cyber & Risk Solution Family, Risk Advisory helps organizations grow with confidence by delivering agile, technology-enabled risk services that strengthen resilience, improve business performance, and unlock new opportunities. We work with complex organizations to assess, transform, and operate internal controls, risk management, compliance and Internal Audit activities, programs, and functions. Participate in Firm activities such as recruiting, training, officewide activities, and more. Other duties as assigned. Why become a Risk Advisory Intern? A Risk Advisory Intern will gain exposure to various industries, business processes, operations, systems and controls as an integral member of project delivery teams. As a Risk Advisory Intern, you will be executing high quality Risk Advisory projects and services under the supervision of experienced Risk Advisory team members. You will be responsible for efficiently managing your workload to budget and timeline. What are we looking for in an Intern? We are seeking self-starters and analytical thinkers who are curious, enjoy working in a collaborative, performance-driven environment, and want to help our clients solve complex problems using the latest technology and data-enabled methods. Ability to work additional hours as needed. Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for employment-based visa sponsorship now or in the future. No visa sponsorship is available for this position. Skill Requirements Ability to learn, understand and work across various industries and functional areas within an organization. Excellent analytical, communication (written and verbal), presentation, and interpersonal skills. Strong technical aptitude, complex analysis, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills. Effective project and time management skills. Ability to work in a rapidly growing, fast-paced, interactive, performance-driven team environment. Enthusiasm to learn through a combination of structured, on-the-job and self-directed training. Ability to work efficiently and effectively independently and in a team environment. Desire to pursue applicable professional license/certification as outlined above. TRAINING: Grant Thornton LLP provides both local and national training programs related to an individual’s job responsibilities. We are committed to ongoing professional development, and we encourage individuals to attend outside training seminars. A strong sense of ownership over one’s own training and development is key to success in this role. The team you’re about to join is ready to help you thrive. Here’s how: Whether it’s your work location, weekly schedule or flex time off, we empower you with the options to work in the way that best serves your clients and your life. Consistent with the firm’s hybrid work model, this position will require in-person attendance at least three days per week, either at a GT office or client site. Here, you are supported to prioritize your overall well-being through work-life integration options that work best for you and those in your household. We are now launching an AI workforce solutions platform designed to help companies turn AI’s potential into practical, measurable business outcomes.Our platform, Assembly Platform, enables teams to design, build, and deploy AI applications, agents, and automations that improve how work gets done. We work side-by-side with clients to identify meaningful use cases, launch solutions, and build the capabilities needed to scale them.This is a fast-moving initiative with executive visibility—and an opportunity to help shape how a new AI solution is positioned, launched, and brought to market. The base salary is one component of Stifel’s overall compensation package for each individual employee. Other benefits and offerings include, but not limited to, discretionary bonuses, health / dental / vision / prescription insurance offerings, Stifel Total Health Connect, flexible spending accounts, tuition & certification assistance programs, paid time off, and much, much more! To view a more comprehensive list of Stifel’s current offerings, please visit https://www.stifel.com/careers/benefits. Applications are accepted until the position is filled.About StifelEaton Partners, a Stifel Company, is one of the oldest, largest and most experienced fund placement agents in the world. The firm’s purpose is to raise institutional capital for investment managers across a full range of alternative strategies – private equity, real assets, real estate and hedge funds/liquid products. In addition, Eaton has a dedicated team focusing on general product advisory, secondaries, and directs. Eaton Partners has participated in raising over $130 billion of institutional capital across more than 175 highly differentiated investment funds. Eaton Partners was acquired by Stifel in January 2016.With over 65 employees in ten offices worldwide, Eaton’s reach is extensive and our dedication to capital raising is unparalleled. jobs.description: Employer: Coursicle Expires: 09/28/2026 Over 2 million college students use Coursicle to stay on top of their classes and homework.Coursicle is your all-in-one academic planner:Sync and color-code assignments from Canvas, Blackboard, Brightspace (D2L), Moodle, and moreGet reminders for upcoming classes, assignments, quizzes, projects, and examsGet notified when classes have open seatsRead reviews of their professorsBuild schedules and create backup schedules for registrationFor the first time since our founding, Coursicle is expanding beyond course registration. This means you'll be responsible for generating user acquisition ideas, testing them, and determining which ones are the most effective. Depending on its effectiveness, content creation may become a core responsibility of this role.UsCompany:700,000 usersRunning entirely on revenueSmall team (6 full-time, 3 part-time)Missions:Mental health: we've seen first-hand the stigma that's held toward mental illness (read our CEO's essay about his struggle with anxiety and depression). Coursicle began as a way to reduce the anxiety of course registration and we're continuing that effort by helping students feel more in control of their academic lives.Wealth disparity: we don't want to make the rich richer, so we don't take investment and we don't optimize for profit. jobs.description: Employer: Federal Reserve Board Expires: 09/28/2026 SummaryThe Federal Reserve Board (Board) provides students opportunities for career success. The Board’s Internship program is designed to provide valuable work experience for graduate students considering careers including, but not limited to, economics, finance and accounting, information systems, and data analysis. The Board believes that by combining academic endeavors with project-related work experience, qualified and capable college students can gain the practical knowledge need in a competitive global job market. Internships are paid positions with salaries commensurate with credit hours; internships may be in-person, remote or hybrid, depending on the needs of the team. Employment in the Board’s internship program is granted to U.S. citizens. Applicants must be currently enrolled in a graduate degree program at an accredited university and returning to continue studies after the internship. Interns have access to a wide range of training programs and events for professional development purposes.Qualifications - ExternalAbout Stress Testing National Program - Operations:The Federal Reserve’s Stress Testing Program assesses whether U.S. bank holding companies (BHCs), covered savings and loan holding companies (SLHCs), and intermediate holding companies of foreign banking organizations (IHCs) with $100 billion or more in assets (together, referred to as “large banks”) are sufficiently capitalized to absorb losses and continue lending to households and businesses under stressful conditions. The stress tests evaluate the resilience of large banks by estimating their losses, revenues, expenses and resulting capital levels - which provide a cushion against losses - under hypothetical recession scenarios into the future.The Stress Testing Operations area includes both Program Management and Technology teams. Together, these teams are responsible for managing the nexus between the Program’s staff, the full scope of assigned work, and accessibility of necessary technology and data. Members of both teams manage cross-functional projects and high-priority initiatives and oversee day-to-day activities to ensure that the Program can meet critical milestones and achieve strategic objectives. jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Property Research & Acquisitions Intern at Centurion Financial Strategies
jobs.description: Employer: Centurion Financial Strategies Expires: 09/28/2026 Description:Are you a naturally persuasive, people-oriented individual who loves talking to people, asking good questions, and figuring out problems that other people avoid?Do you have an entrepreneurial streak—and perhaps find the idea of investigating deceased owners, missing heirs, unpaid taxes, family mysteries, and forgotten properties strangely fascinating?Join our family-run land investment company and help us uncover valuable opportunities hidden inside properties with complicated ownership situations.We are a successful vacant land investment business that has recently expanded into the world of “messy title” real estate. These are properties that may have deceased owners, multiple heirs, unpaid property taxes, unresolved estates, family disagreements, or other ownership complications.Most investors look at these properties and run away.We look at them and say, “Well…this is interesting.”As a Messy Title Acquisitions Intern, you will initially focus heavily on cold calling potential property owners and heirs. You may also follow up with leads generated through online advertising, direct mail, and other marketing campaigns. In addition, you will help research properties, ownership histories, family relationships, court records, and other information that helps us determine whether an opportunity is worth pursuing.This is not an internship where you quietly reorganize spreadsheets in a dark corner while everyone forgets your name.You will have real conversations with real people about real properties. You will learn sales, negotiation, real estate investing, lead generation, title research, and how entrepreneurs identify opportunities that most people completely miss.This position is perfect for someone who is incredibly personable, naturally inclined toward sales, competitive, curious, and excited by the possibility of helping build something from the ground up.Your mission in this position is to start conversations, build trust, uncover the real story behind each property, consistently follow up with potential sellers, and help turn overlooked leads into profitable real estate opportunities.What We’re Looking For in a Team Member:We value candidates who resonate with our core values:💡 Professional Conduct – We treat everyone with respect and integrity, keeping communication professional and timely.📈 Continually Pursuing Growth – We’re always improving, learning, and adapting to become better at what we do.🤝 Team-First Attitude – We collaborate, support, and have each other’s backs—we win together.💙 Drive to Serve Others – Whether it’s clients, partners, or teammates, we always go the extra mile.📬 Follow-Up in Communication – We’re pleasantly persistent, ensuring nothing gets lost in the shuffle.✅ Reliability – We do what we say we will, meeting deadlines and staying accountable.🚀 Proactive Effort – We take ownership of our work, anticipate challenges, and solve problems before they happen.🌎 Flexibility – Things change, and we adapt to keep moving forward.Do these ring true with your soul—and does the idea of getting paid to solve real estate mysteries sound more interesting than making coffee and alphabetizing folders?Keep reading. Key Responsibilities:Make outbound cold calls to potential property owners, heirs, and other interested parties.Build rapport with people from a wide variety of backgrounds and family situations.Ask thoughtful questions to uncover the story behind a property and its ownership.Follow up diligently and consistently with potential sellers through phone, text, email, and other communication tools.Respond to and follow up with leads generated through online advertising, direct mail, and other marketing campaigns.Qualify and categorize leads based on motivation, ownership, property value, occupancy, family circumstances, and other relevant factors.Manage and update leads in the CRM system.Research property ownership, deeds, tax records, court cases, obituaries, probate records, family relationships, and potential heirs.Help construct basic family trees and ownership timelines.Set appointments and move qualified opportunities forward to the appropriate team member.Collaborate with the team to improve scripts, research methods, sales processes, and follow-up systems.Occasionally assist with other business areas as needed.Help us build a messy title acquisitions department that currently has more opportunity than hands available to pursue it.Skills & Qualifications:Strong communication and interpersonal skills.Naturally personable and comfortable starting conversations with strangers.A genuine interest in sales, negotiation, entrepreneurship, or real estate.Comfortable making cold calls and hearing “no” without needing to lie down for the rest of the afternoon.Curious and willing to ask good follow-up questions.Able to listen carefully and identify important details during conversations.Detail-oriented and a strong problem solver.Highly proactive, competitive, and results-driven.Persistent without being pushy or disrespectful.Comfortable using technology and learning new software.Able to conduct online research and organize information clearly.Willing to receive coaching, practice scripts, review calls, and continually improve.Able to handle conversations involving deceased family members, unpaid taxes, family disagreements, and other potentially sensitive situations with empathy and professionalism.Previous sales experience is helpful but not necessarily required. A strong natural sales ability, confidence, curiosity, and willingness to learn may be even more important.An entrepreneurial mindset is extremely important. We want someone who notices opportunities, takes ownership, and wants to help build something—not someone who needs to be handed a checklist every fifteen minutes.Schedule and Location:Approximately 15–20 hours per week.A minimum of eight hours per week must be completed in our Twin Cities-area office.Ideally, most or all working hours would be completed in the office so you can learn directly from the team, receive coaching, and participate in live deal discussions.We may be open to some flexible or remote hours after trust, consistency, and performance have been established.Saturday and Sunday hours may be available for the right person.Some evening or weekend calling may occasionally be helpful because property owners tend to have an annoying habit of working during normal business hours.What We Offer:$14 per hour.A results-oriented commission equal to 10% of the gross profit on properties you directly help acquire, paid after the property sells.Real-world sales experience—not role-playing exercises that disappear into a professor’s filing cabinet.Hands-on training in cold calling, negotiation, real estate acquisitions, property research, genealogy, title issues, and distressed property investing.Direct mentoring from the company’s owners and experienced team members.The opportunity to participate in actual deals and see the financial results of your work.A supportive, close-knit team environment.Significant room to grow for someone who performs well and embraces responsibility.The possibility of this internship developing into a full-time position for the right person.The long-term opportunity to help lead and build our messy title acquisitions department.For an exceptional person who creates substantial value over time, there may even be an opportunity to participate in company ownership far into the future.To be clear, we are not promising that someone will work here for three months, acquire two properties, and receive the keys to the kingdom.However, we believe strongly in rewarding people who think like owners, produce meaningful results, earn trust, and help us build something valuable.Who This Position Is Probably Not For:This position probably is not for you if:You are terrified of talking to strangers.You give up after one unanswered call.You believe following up twice qualifies as “being persistent.”You need every hour of your day mapped out for you.You want an internship that looks impressive on paper but does not require you to produce anything.You dislike sales, competition, accountability, or measurable results.You regularly say, “That’s not my job.”You would rather avoid a difficult problem than become the person who knows how to solve it.This position may be an outstanding fit if you are hungry, coachable, persuasive, curious, and excited by the idea of learning how real businesses and real estate deals are actually built.How to Apply:Send us an email with:Your resume.A brief introduction about yourself.Your answer to: What appeals to you about this job, and why do you think you would be a great fit?Tell us about a time you persuaded someone, sold something, started a project, or found a creative solution to a difficult problem.Include your general availability and whether you are available to work occasional evenings or weekends.Bonus: Include a short audio or video clip “selling us” on why you would excel in this role.Do not spend three hours creating a cinematic masterpiece. We mostly want to hear how you communicate, whether you can hold someone’s attention, and whether your personality comes through.Start your email with the phrase:“Meet your new family member [Your Name]”This demonstrates your attention to detail and prevents your application from immediately disappearing into the mysterious land where applicants who do not follow directions go.About Us:We are a small but successful land flipping firm. We’ve been in business since 2017 and have built a seven-figure revenue business. We have continued to grow each and every year so far.We use direct mail, cold calling, online advertising, and other marketing campaigns to acquire land and distressed properties at a discount from sellers who may live far away, no longer use the property, inherited it, fell behind on taxes, or simply do not know how to resolve the situation.After purchasing, we work through the problems, prepare the property for resale, and sell it closer to market value.The best way to describe our traditional land business is this:We buy from the people who see it as trash and sell it to the people who see it as treasure.Our messy title business takes that idea one step further.We look for properties that other investors overlook because the ownership is confusing, the family situation is complicated, or the research requires more patience than most people are willing to give it.Our job is to find the people involved, understand the problem, treat them fairly, and determine whether we can create a solution where everyone wins.A Note From Dave:I am one of the owners, Dave, and if this sounds fascinating to you, we’d love to learn more about you.This business has been a blessing to my family and so many others, and I take it seriously. I started the business in 2017 and believe in having multiple streams of income. I would love to take the right person under my wing and teach them not only how to perform this job, but how to think like an entrepreneur, salesperson, investor, and future leader.They say your spouse is the only family member you get to choose. However, our small team is a family, and I’ll get to choose you!Some facts about me are the following:I’m the dad of two amazing girls—one in college and one finishing junior high—and husband to my even more amazing wife. I live in the Twin Cities area and love being outside running, walking, hiking, or biking.I’m also a total nerd who loves reading fantasy books—check out Michael J. Sullivan; he’s awesome—as well as business books. I enjoy playing World War 3: Conflict of Nations on my phone, and on occasion, I have been known to break a few windows when I try to sing.I am genuinely excited about building this department. I believe the right intern could learn an enormous amount, make a meaningful contribution, earn commissions from actual properties, and potentially build a career that extends far beyond a normal college internship.We have a few websites for you to peruse to learn about us and our values as a company:www.genfamproperties.comOur selling sitewww.genfamland.comOne of our buying sitesAlso, check out our YouTube channel:https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCqGNtIx9she_-74Cq7fnzvg

jobs.description: Employer: PIMCO Expires: 09/28/2026 PIMCO is a global leader in active fixed income. In the 50+ years since, we have worked relentlessly to help millions of investors pursue their objectives – regardless of shifting marketing conditions. As active investors, our goal is not just to find opportunities, but to create them. To this end, we remain firmly committed to the pursuit of our mission: delivering superior investment returns, solutions, and service to our clients. Since 1971, our people have shaped our organization through a high-performance inclusive culture, in which we celebrate diverse thinking. We invest in our people and strive to imprint our CORE values of Collaboration, Openness, Responsibility and Excellence. We believe each of us is here to help others succeed and this has led to PIMCO being recognized as an innovator, industry thought leader and trusted advisor to our clients. 2027 Summer Internship - Global Wealth Management, Growth Markets, US Positions are located in New York, NY. Global Wealth Management (GWM)’s mission is to create industry leading experiences for financial intermediaries and their individual investor clients while providing a strong contribution to PIMCO’s overall business results. PIMCO GWM is responsible for business strategy and client coverage for financial intermediaries and their advisors. Coverage includes RIAs, Wirehouses, family offices, banks/trusts, independent broker dealers, platforms, and sub-advisory relationships. You're eligible to apply if you: Pursuing an undergraduate degree Must be able to begin full time employment from a PIMCO office between January 2028 – August 2028 Must be enrolled at a university during the Fall 2027 semester (August 2027 – December 2027) Have a minimum 3.5 cumulative collegiate grade point average on a 4.0 scale (or the equivalent) at an accredited 4-year college or university Are business proficient in English You'll excel as a Global Wealth Management Account Analyst if you: Show strong interest in the financial markets, macroeconomics, and investment finance Have the ability to articulate ideas/strategies clearly, both verbally and in writing Demonstrate a strong interest in fixed income markets, investment products, and business strategy, with curiosity for product innovation and evolving client needs Possess the ability to develop client relationships into strategic partnerships and interest in client facing career within Finance Are personable, ethical, collaborative, organized, flexible, high energy, self-starter, accountable, humble Have the ability to multi-task and handle several projects delivering completed work within expected timeline Demonstrate high level of proficiency with Microsoft Excel and Powerpoint Have Finance/capital markets coursework (recommended, not required) Demonstrate curiosity and experience in using new emerging technologies and AI tools in your work or school projects to solve problems and drive better outcomes Growth Markets: The Growth Markets group focuses on accelerating growth across product lines with unique technology, service, and operational needs beyond our core mutual fund franchise. The group is responsible for leading business strategy, innovation, and growth initiatives across SMAs, ETFs, Models, Insurance Solutions, and Blockchain/Tokenization. The summer analyst intern will contribute to the team through supporting the group’s key strategic initiatives. While our eligibility requirements are not flexible, we encourage you to apply even if you do not possess 100% of the desired skills outlined above. jobs.description: Employer: NeuroSync Expires: 09/29/2026 Clinical Research Intern (Diagnostics) PLEASE ONLY APPLY IF YOU LIVE/GO TO SCHOOL IN MAPLEASE ONLY APPLY IF YOU HAVE PRIOR INTERNSHIP/WORK EXPERIENCERISING JUNIOR/SENIOR PREFERRED 📍 Location: Holliston, MA → In-Person⏳ Duration: Fall 2026 (Full-Time, 10-12 Weeks)💰 Compensation: Stipend ($2–4k based on time and performance) About the Role:We are seeking a detail-oriented Clinical Research Intern to join our team. This role sits at the intersection of neurology, ophthalmology, and data science. This role will assist in literature research expanding our diagnostic application for diverse pathologies from cognitive impairment to ADHD.The Clinical Research Intern will review medical literature and market application of our related technologies . Expanding our diagnostic library, identifying how distinct ocular-motor signatures can differentiate between a wide spectrum of neurological and systemic conditions. About Us:NeuroSync is at the forefront of neurotechnology innovation, offering a digital health platform designed for the assessment of brain health, the management of recovery processes, and the optimization of performance. Our mission is to leverage next-generation technologies to enhance understanding and care for neurological conditions, providing solutions that cater to individuals and professionals alike.While traditional diagnostics rely on subjective patient reporting, NeuroSync utilizes high-fidelity eye-tracking biomarkers to provide objective, physiological evidence of brain health. Eye-tracking technology is increasingly used as a "window into the brain" for neurodegenerative diseases, vestibular disorders, and even mental health conditions. By analyzing the neural pathways that control eye movement, we can detect "micro-errors" that indicate specific types of brain dysfunction. This role will support research into how eye-tracking technology serves as a diagnostic tool for:Neurodegenerative Diseases: Identifying research biomarkers for ADHD, Parkinson’s and Alzheimer’s.Mild Traumatic Brain Injury (mTBI): Mapping vestibular-ocular reflex (VOR) impairments in concussion recovery.Neurodevelopmental Disorders: Refining protocols for ADHD and Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) through gaze-pattern analysis.Psychiatric Monitoring: Investigating correlations between ocular pursuit and conditions such as Schizophrenia or severe Depression.Fatigue & Performance: Analyzing microsaccades to measure cognitive load and neurological readiness in high-performance athletes or pilots. Key ResponsibilitiesMultivariate Data Collection: Assist in literature research expanding our diagnostic application for diverse pathologies from cognitive impairment to ADHD.Advanced Biomarker Analysis: Research and analyze specific patterns such as Saccadic Latency, Hypometria (undershooting targets), and Nystagmus (involuntary oscillation).Literature Reviews: Synthesize peer-reviewed research on the "eye-brain" connection, focusing on the cranial nerves and brainstem regions involved in ocular-motor controlData Integrity: Maintain clinical databases ensuring HIPAA-compliant storage of high-resolution biometric data. Requirements:Residency in Massachusetts (MA) or currently attending university in MAAvailability to work on-site at our office Mon–FriInterest in health economics, healthcare policy, Excellent research, writing, and analytical skillsAbility to work independently, manage multiple tasks, and meet deadlines Job Type:Full-time, 10–12 week internship. Compensation based on skills and experience.

jobs.description: Employer: Agate Publishing, Inc. Expires: 09/29/2026 Agate is seeking interns for its six-month on-site internship program. The internship terms are typically between January 1–June 30 (we are accepting applications now for 2027 candidates) and July 1–December 31 (we have filled these spots for 2026 and are now seeking candidates only for early 2027). Interns are asked to spend approximately 20-30 hours per week on site, depending on their availability, and receive extensive training as well as credit from their academic institution and a stipend of approximately $80 per week. We offer interns considerable flexibility in scheduling their hours during the work week, to allow them to attend school and/or hold paying jobs while also doing the internship. Agate accepts applications for internships year-round.Agate has an excellent record in helping interns find publishing industry jobs, whether in the Chicago area or elsewhere. Several Agate interns have been offered staff positions and contractor roles at the company, though there is no formal, structured intern hiring program here, and no interns are guaranteed jobs after completing the program. Most of the Agate staff who oversee our internship program have themselves been Agate interns. All Agate interns are trained in a variety of fundamental publishing and small business tasks, with an eye toward preparing them for different entry-level job opportunities in publishing. All Agate interns participate in eight intensive, in-depth training seminars during the course of the internship, for which they earn a Publishing Basics certification from our Agate Publishing Academy division. These seminars are designed to give interns a 360-degree understanding of basic trade and educational publishing functions by the time they complete the program.Qualifications: Agate only considers candidates who have completed at least half their junior year of undergraduate studies. Preference is given to enrolled students, whether undergraduate or graduate, who are able to earn credit for their Agate training internship. Strong reading, writing, and personal communication skills are essential, as is a solid grasp of English grammar and style. Previous experience in manuscript editing and/or familiarity with The Chicago Manual of Style is very welcome. Solid organizational skills and computer skills are also desired. Experience with the Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, InDesign) is a bonus but not required.The internship may entail some or all of the following responsibilities:Produce catalog and press materials, including press kits and pitches Draft and send out mass mailings Assist with publicity campaigns by communicating via email with media organizationsAssist in pre-publication market research Compile and organize media contact information Produce social media postings Help maintain office inventory Write, edit, and post website informationRead and review manuscript submissions Copyedit, proofread, and review educational and marketing contentWrite and research assessment and manuscript content Perform administrative and organizational tasksTo apply: Email a resume, cover letter, and two nonfiction writing samples, amounting to no more than 3000 words total, and—if you wish to demonstrate design experience—two design samples in PDF format, no larger than 2MB, to onsite@agatepublishing.com, with the words “On-Site Internship Application” in the subject line of the message.

jobs.description: Employer: Wells Fargo Expires: 09/30/2026 About this role: Wells Fargo is seeking talent to join the Human Resources (HR) organization for a 2027 summer internship. Learn more about the career areas and lines of business at wellsfargojobs.com. Program Overview:Human Resources (HR) at Wells Fargo is a centralized function that is aligned with and supports the company, lines of business, and enterprise functions. The HR organization is responsible for building and implementing strategies, programs, and infrastructure to identify, develop, and retain top talent for the company. To achieve these goals, the organization spans across a wide range of areas, including but not limited to: Total Rewards, Governance & Workforce Relations, HR Operations & Service Delivery, Talent Acquisition, Transformation & Product, and Talent Management & Learning.As part of our commitment to developing the leaders of tomorrow, we are proud to offer the Human Resources Internship Program. You will begin your ten-week experience with a robust induction week orientation and training, and then launch into your internship assignment. During your time as an HR Intern, you will have on-the-job experiences, program management support, access to senior leaders and mentorship, and ongoing learning opportunities to help guide your career path. This program is designed to provide undergraduate students with a blend of business and professional development training opportunities that incorporate real-world experiences and prepare you for a career in HR at Wells Fargo.To ensure a well-rounded experience, the Human Resources Internship Program will consist of experiences anchored in the following competencies with an emphasis on critical thinking and technical skill development:AdvisoryData & AnalyticsExecution & DeliveryProcess ManagementRisk & ComplianceSolutions Design & Development In this role you will:Perform a variety of job assignments to develop key skills and gain a working knowledge of the organizationAttend classroom training, self-study assignments, workshops, networking, and other eventsParticipate in or provide support for low complexity initiatives within functional areaReview basic or tactical issues, policies or procedures for which answers can be quickly obtained related to low-risk tasks and deliverables with narrower impactReceive direction from supervisor and exercise judgment within defined parameters while developing understanding of the function, policies, procedures, and compliance requirementsProvide information to managers, functional colleagues, and stakeholders, including internal or external customers if applicable Required Qualifications:6+ months of work experience, or equivalent demonstrated through one or a combination of the following: work experience, training, military experience, education Desired Qualifications:Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree with an expected graduation date between December 2027 – June 2028 in the fields of Human Resources Management, Business, Finance, Organizational Psychology, or Analytics. All majors are welcomeStrong critical thinking and data analysis skills, with the ability to generate insights, learn quickly, adapt to change, and support innovative HR solutionsFamiliarity with AI‑powered productivity tools (such as chat‑based assistants and built‑in features like Microsoft Copilot) to support everyday tasks including research, organizing information, and creating presentations with a strong interest in learning and using these tools responsiblyAbility to execute with urgency, support business reporting, project coordination, and solution delivery, and contribute to operational excellence with an enterprise mindsetStrong communication and stakeholder relationship skills, with the ability to foster an inclusive environment and actively seek and apply feedback to support effective HR collaborationStrong business acumen and service orientation, with the ability to understand HR needs and support solutions that deliver a positive employee and business impactAbility to act with integrity, apply HR policies and compliance requirements, and support effective risk controls to maintain well-managed and compliant HR operations Program Locations: Charlotte, NC Pay Range: $33.66 - $33.66/hr. Program duration: 10 weeks; June – August 2027; High‑performing interns may be considered for a full‑time offer into the HR Development Program upon graduation Wells Fargo only considers candidates who are presently authorized to work for any employer in the United States and who do not require work visa sponsorship from Wells Fargo now or in the future in order to retain their authorization to work in the United States.Based on the volume of applications received, this job posting may be removed prior to the indicated close date. After submitting your application, please monitor your e-mail for future communications. Posting End Date: 29 Sep 2026*Job posting may come down early due to volume of applicants. We Value Equal OpportunityWells Fargo is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other legally protected characteristic.Employees support our focus on building strong customer relationships balanced with a strong risk mitigating and compliance-driven culture which firmly establishes those disciplines as critical to the success of our customers and company. They are accountable for execution of all applicable risk programs (Credit, Market, Financial Crimes, Operational, Regulatory Compliance), which includes effectively following and adhering to applicable Wells Fargo policies and procedures, appropriately fulfilling risk and compliance obligations, timely and effective escalation and remediation of issues, and making sound risk decisions. There is emphasis on proactive monitoring, governance, risk identification and escalation, as well as making sound risk decisions commensurate with the business unit’s risk appetite and all risk and compliance program requirements.Candidates applying to job openings posted in Canada: Applications for employment are encouraged from all qualified candidates, including women, persons with disabilities, aboriginal peoples and visible minorities. Accommodation for applicants with disabilities is available upon request in connection with the recruitment process. jobs.description: Employer: Rapid Response Monitoring Services Expires: 09/30/2026 LocationThis position is 100% in-office and reports to our facility on site in Syracuse, NY. Job SummaryAs an Accounting Intern, you will support the accounting and finance team by performing daily clerical tasks, assisting with financial record-keeping, and gaining hands on experience with accounting procedures. Pay Range$22.50 per hour Hours: Fall & Spring Part-TimeSchedule varies based on candidate availability ResponsibilitiesPrimary duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to:Assisting the Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Financial or Tax teams with various tasks.Provide support to the financial team for month end and year end closing activities.Prepare supporting documentation for audits and financial reporting.Organize and file financial documents (digital and physical).Update accounting database and reconciliations with current information.Perform account reconciliations and identify and report discrepancies.Support the Tax team in gathering and organizing financial data for compliance and audit purposes.Perform tax research on regulatory updates and summarize findings for management.Help prepare supporting schedules and documentation for tax filings and financial audits.Maintain accurate and confidential tax records.Assist with sales tax, property tax, and payroll tax compliance as needed.Participate in special projects related to tax planning or process improvement. Founded and headquartered in Syracuse since 1992, with offices in California and Nevada. Our growing organization serves as a critical response center focused on protecting life, residences, and businesses. Whether it’s a kitchen fire, an intruder at a business, a family member experiencing a medical emergency, or preventative non-emergency customer service conversations, our heroes are here to serve every day - 24/7, 365 days a year. Supported by teams of experts in their respective fields, our highly trained specialists are the monitoring backbone for thousands of alarm companies across the country. If you are in search of a unique, rewarding career opportunity in an industry like no other, join #TeamRapid! Located in Franklin Square, Rapid Response prides itself as a newly remodeled state-of-the-art facility containing ultra-modern technology. From touch-free entrances and continual sanitization to iPad break rooms and comfortable lounge areas, our employees enjoy a pristine and contemporary work environment. Additional InformationRapid Response offers a competitive compensation and benefits package and dynamic and professional work environments. We also offer continued growth through our internal advancement opportunities. For more information, view our website at https://www.rrms.com/careers/. Rapid Response is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
